about: Crisis wargames (doc 126): a scenario is a timeline of injects — a thing that happens (an agency sends a requisition, a bank asks for a recall, the press calls, a second incident lands, a key person is unavailable) — each owned by a team, each with an expected action and a deadline (SLA). You run it as a tabletop, respond to each inject, and the estate scores whether the right action reached the right team in time, then writes an after-action report with the coordination gaps and the improvement actions. Worst-case is built in: colliding deadlines, missing people, a second hit mid-response. Deliberately generic — no organisation, person or case. The library is data; add your own scenarios and injects. Scoring is deterministic (keyword rubric); when a gateway is configured it also asks a model to grade the free-text and to play the inject's sender, inheriting the rails and the audit trail. Not a substitute for a real exercise programme; a frictionless way to practise the coordination every week.

payment-fraud.name: Payment-rail fraud, multi-agency
payment-fraud.about: Fraudulent outward payments are discovered at reconciliation. Within hours a sectoral CERT, the financial regulator and the police are all involved — and the coordination, not the attack, decides the outcome.
worst_case: the deadlines of two agencies collide
the single person who knows the rail is on leave
a second batch of fraud lands while you respond

injects.text: Daily reconciliation shows the settlement account is short; outward payments do not match the core ledger.
injects.expect: declare an incident; start the regulator clock and the crisis requisitions; do not let more payments go

injects.text: More outward messages are queued for release in the next window. Who can stop them, and will you?
injects.expect: stop or hold outward release; name who has authority; record the decision
injects.hint: decision note; recall/hold request to beneficiary banks

injects.text: The CERT requires forensic artefacts from the affected servers within 6 hours.
injects.expect: get the tool-exception signed; collect volatile data first with chain-of-custody; keep the clock

injects.text: A beneficiary bank asks for written confirmation before it will hold the funds.
injects.expect: send the recall/hold request with the transaction schedule in a separate secure attachment; get acknowledgement

injects.text: A journalist calls: 'We hear your bank has been hacked and customer money is gone. Comment?'
injects.expect: one holding statement, one spokesperson; facts only, no speculation, no numbers; route all media to comms

injects.text: WORST CASE: the one engineer who understands the rail is on leave and unreachable.
injects.expect: activate the deputy / vendor under the retainer; do not let a single person be the dependency
injects.hint: ./securax crisis comms vendor-activation; name a deputy

injects.text: The police serve a production notice: a long schedule of records, each from a different team, due in 72 hours.
injects.expect: open the production-notice requisition; auto-prepare what the estate holds; assign and chase the rest
injects.hint: ./securax crisis new le-production-notice; ./securax crisis auto; ./securax crisis watch

injects.text: WORST CASE: the regulator's initial-report deadline and the CERT artefact deadline fall within the same hour.
injects.expect: parallelise across teams; do not serialise; the clock shows both — file the regulator report, hand the CERT pack, in parallel

ransomware.name: Ransomware, data-centre wide
ransomware.about: Systems are encrypted and a ransom note appears; backups are a target. The test is whether containment, a clean restore, the regulator clock and the comms all move at once without a single coordinator becoming the bottleneck.
worst_case: the newest backup is also encrypted
a node that holds the incident clock goes down
staff start posting on social media

injects.text: Multiple servers are encrypted; a ransom note is on the screens. What is the first move?
injects.expect: declare the incident; isolate affected hosts (do not power off — preserve memory); start the clock and the playbook
injects.hint: ./securax crisis start ransomware  ·  ./securax playbook start ransomware

injects.text: WORST CASE: the newest backup is also encrypted. Do you still have a clean copy?
injects.expect: prove a CLEAN off-site copy exists before restoring (ransomguard checks it); never pay first

injects.text: Employees are asking what happened; some are posting on social media.
injects.expect: send the staff alert: stop external talk and social posts; one source of truth; route media to comms

injects.text: The CERT wants the first incident report in 6 hours and forensic artefacts to follow.
injects.expect: file the initial report; begin forensic collection with authority and chain-of-custody
injects.hint: ./securax crisis start ransomware (opens the CERT requisition)  ·  incident due

injects.text: WORST CASE: the machine holding the incident clock goes down mid-response.
injects.expect: another node already has the open incident read-only; continue from there — no single point of failure

injects.text: The regulator asks whether customer-facing services are up, and when they will be.
injects.expect: give the service status and the restore ETA; a customer service notice; no over-commitment
